messages:
Devon H: Heads-up — saw a weird spike on the per-route token-latency dashboard for /chat/model-x around 14:11 UTC. SM occupancy dropped to ~12% while VRAM usage jumped +8GB.
Ajay P: Hmm. Did the kernel selector fallback at that time? Generic kernels can blow up VRAM and latency.
Devon H: I checked the logs quickly. kernel-selector flagged a fallback at 14:11:53 for model-x-ggml when batch shapes mixed, then fell back to generic_attn_v2.
```
[14:11:53] kernel_selector: fallback -> generic_attn_v2 for model=model-x-ggml seq=1024 batch=3
```
Maria L: That would explain lower SM occupancy but higher memory temp allocations — generic kernels are less SM-efficient and often allocate bigger scratch buffers.
Sophie R: Also check KVCACHE_MISS around the same window. If kvcache got evicted, tail latency will pop.
Ajay P: Can someone run a quick PromQL to correlate? Suggested queries:
```
sum(rate(kvcache_miss_total[1m])) by (model)
avg_over_time(gpu_sm_occupancy[5m])
```
Devon H: Ran the queries on the timeframe. model-x kvcache misses spiked x3 at 14:11, sm occupancy variance high, and MIG slice usage for gpu-node-42 jumped.
Kevin M: Slice reallocation mid-flight is unlikely, but a preemptible/ephemeral job on the same host could have caused fragmentation. Which node was it?
Devon H: gpu-node-42 in us-west2-slice2.
ops-bot: Note: Preemptible batch job id=99321 started on gpu-node-42 at 14:09 UTC and consumed 6GB temporarily.
Maria L: OK, hypothesis: mixed-seqlen coalescing -> kernel selector chooses fallback generic kernel -> larger per-invocation scratch -> VRAM pressure -> KVCACHE evictions -> kvcache misses -> token-tail latency. Also multi-tenant preemptible workload made node fragmented so generic kernel allocations couldn't be packed.
Sophie R: Agreed. For instrumentation/dashboarding we should add route-aware token-level KPIs and kernel-selector metrics. Panels to add:
- per-route token p50/p95/p99 heatmap
- kvcache hit/miss rate by route and model
- kernel-selector fallback count by model + reason tag
- SM occupancy variance heatmap per node and per MIG slice
- VRAM transient allocation spikes (allocs/sec)
Also annotate panels with preemptible job events.
Devon H: I'll draft a Grafana panel set. Example PromQL for token p95 by route:
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, route) (rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])))
```
Ajay P: Also add derived KPI: cost_per_token = (avg_gpu_power_watts * invocation_duration_s) / tokens_generated. Useful to measure unit economics when kernel path changes.
Kevin M: Short-term mitigations:
- Force kernel-selector to prefer quant-friendly kernels for model-x on the us-west2 slice pool
- Pin /chat/model-x traffic to dedicated pool while we investigate
- Add a small runtime patch to avoid fallback on mixed-shape micro-batches (canary on staging)
Maria L: Long-term: make batcher slice-aware — avoid coalescing across MIG slice boundaries and prefer uniform seq-len groups, and add preemptible job annotations in the autoscaler events stream.
Sophie R: I'll implement dashboard panels and export the panel json. Sharing once ready.
Devon H: Created PERF-1287 with checklist: reproduce on staging, dashboard panels, kernel-selector patch, canary rollout.
Ajay P: Add alert: if kernel_selector_fallback_count > 3/m for any model -> page eng-runtime.
ops-bot: Alert rule "kernel-selector-fallback-high" created in staging.
Devon H: Thanks all, will follow-up with panel links and a short RCA after 24h requery. :thumbsup:
Sophie R: FYI I'll include a small example dashboard layout: left col = per-route tails, center = kernel/kvcache correlations, right = node-level SM/VRAM/MIG.
Kevin M: If needed I can temporarily add a node pool label to routing so we can quickly pin traffic for experiments.
Devon H: Perfect — assigning owners in the ticket.
